title: A finite family of pseudo-coherent localizations has a finite-free model
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a cochain complex of $A$-modules, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$ a finite family, possibly empty. Fix derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] of modules over all $A_{f_j}$. Suppose every $Q(M_{f_j})$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. There exist a complex $F$ of $A$-modules, an integer $b$ such that $F^i=0$ for $i>b$, finite free terms $F^i$, and a chain map $\alpha:F\to M$ such that $\alpha_{f_j}$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $j$. The family is not required to generate the unit ideal.

proof.text: Choose finite-free bounded-above models for the finitely many localizations from ring pseudo-coherence. Take a common upper cohomology bound b (any b for the empty family). Start with F=0, alpha=0 at cutoff n=b+1. Maintain F zero below n and above b, finite free, and localized cohomology isomorphisms above n and surjections in degree n. The localized cones are then zero in cohomology in degrees at least n by the cone long exact sequence.

At each step localized F is bounded finite free, hence (n)-pseudo-coherent. A stupid truncation of the local bounded-above free model of M is (n-1)-pseudo-coherent. Apply the cone pseudo-coherence lemma at m=n-1, then finite top cohomology, to conclude that every localized cone has finite cohomology in degree n-1.

For each localization choose finitely many generators of its degree-(n-1) cone cohomology and cycle representatives. Express each representative as x/f_j^a. Since d(x) becomes zero after localization, f_j^c d(x)=0 for some c. Replace x by f_j^c x, an actual global cycle; its localized class is the original generator times the unit f_j^(a+c). The finitely many representatives over all j define a map from a finite free A-module to cone cycles, surjecting on cohomology at every localization. Split its cone coordinates into the new map component and the negative differential. The cycle equation proves the two complex identities. Adjoin this module in degree n-1. The cone triangle cohomology sequence gives localized isomorphisms in degrees at least n and surjectivity in n-1; higher degrees are unchanged.

Iterate the preceding extension along n=b+1-k for natural k. Use compatible extensions whose components in previously constructed degrees are retained. Define each final term and differential from any sufficiently late stage; compatibility makes these independent of the stage. They satisfy the square-zero and chain-map equations at that stage. All terms above b vanish and every term is finite free. For each cohomology degree i choose a stage past i-1, so that the three terms computing H^i have stabilized and the stage map is a localized cohomology isomorphism in degree i. Thus every final localized map is a quasi-isomorphism. For an empty family take F=0. No global finiteness of the cone cohomology or global cohomology vanishing is used.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_localization_free_model (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    [∀ i : Fin r, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.Away (f i)))]
    (hlocal : ∀ i : Fin r, IsPseudoCoherent
      (Q.obj ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f i))))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M))) :
    ∃ (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (b : ℤ), F.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free A (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite A (F.X i)) ∧
      ∃ α : F ⟶ M, ∀ j : Fin r, QuasiIso
        ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (f j))))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α)
